name: Taj Mahal, Agra
notes: A white marble mausoleum on the banks of the Yamuna, built as a tribute of love and widely regarded as one of the finest examples of Mughal architecture. The symmetry of the gardens, the changing light on the marble through the day, and the intricate inlay work make it a place that rewards slow, repeated viewing.

name: Qutub Minar, Delhi
notes: A tall sandstone and marble minaret surrounded by an ancient complex of ruins, tombs and carved archways. Walking through the grounds gives a strong sense of Delhi's layered history, with each courtyard revealing another detail from a different century.

name: Konark Sun Temple, Odisha
notes: A 13th-century temple built in the form of a giant stone chariot, with carved wheels and horses along its base. The scale and detail of the stonework make it one of the most striking examples of temple architecture on the eastern coast.

name: Khajuraho Temples, Madhya Pradesh
notes: A group of medieval temples known for their elaborate carvings covering nearly every surface. The complex is spread across open lawns, making it easy to walk between structures and notice how the carving style shifts from one temple to the next.

name: Mysore Palace, Karnataka
notes: A grand royal palace known for its domes, arches and richly decorated interiors. The building is especially memorable when lit up in the evening, when thousands of bulbs outline its entire structure against the night sky.

name: Golden Temple, Amritsar
notes: The holiest Sikh shrine, with a gold-plated sanctum sitting in the middle of a large reflective pool. The calm pace of the pilgrims, the constant recitation of hymns and the communal kitchen feeding thousands daily all add to the atmosphere.

name: Ajanta Caves, Maharashtra
notes: A series of rock-cut Buddhist caves carved into a horseshoe-shaped cliff, containing paintings and sculptures dating back over two thousand years. The setting above a river gorge makes the approach itself part of the experience.

name: Ellora Caves, Maharashtra
notes: A complex of Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut monuments carved into a single basalt cliff. The Kailasa temple here, cut entirely from a single rock, is one of the most ambitious ancient construction projects in the country.

name: Meenakshi Temple, Madurai
notes: A vast temple complex with towering, brightly painted gopurams covered in thousands of carved figures. The inner corridors, pillared halls and constant flow of pilgrims make it feel like a small town built entirely within temple walls.

name: Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh
notes: A former Mughal capital built entirely of red sandstone, now preserved as a ghost city of palaces, courtyards and gateways. Despite being abandoned soon after it was built, the architecture remains remarkably intact.

name: Valley of Flowers, Uttarakhand
notes: A high-altitude Himalayan valley that bursts into colour with wildflowers during the monsoon months. The short trekking season and remote location make reaching it feel like a reward in itself.

name: Dudhsagar Falls, Goa
notes: A four-tiered waterfall dropping through dense forest along the Goa-Karnataka border, often seen from a passing train as well as from the base. The spray and volume of water are strongest just after the monsoon.

name: Sundarbans Mangrove Forest, West Bengal
notes: The world's largest mangrove forest, crisscrossed by tidal rivers and home to the Bengal tiger. Boat journeys through the narrow channels reveal a landscape that shifts completely with the tide.

name: Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu
notes: A range of rolling blue-tinted hills covered in tea plantations, shola forests and winding mountain roads. The mix of cool climate and layered viewpoints makes it a favourite for slow drives and short walks alike.

name: Chilika Lake, Odisha
notes: Asia's largest brackish water lagoon, known for migratory birds in winter and resident Irrawaddy dolphins near its mouth. The shifting boundary between lake and sea gives the area a constantly changing character.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park, Manipur
notes: The only floating national park in the world, built on a thick mat of vegetation over Loktak Lake. It is the last natural home of the endangered sangai deer, which appears to walk on water from a distance.

name: Dal Lake, Srinagar
notes: A large lake lined with houseboats, floating gardens and shikaras moving slowly across the water. Watching the early morning floating vegetable market is one of the more unusual ways to start a day here.

name: Marine Drive, Mumbai
notes: A long curved promenade along the Arabian Sea, often called the Queen's Necklace for the way its streetlights trace the coastline at night. It draws joggers, couples and street vendors in equal measure through the day.

name: Pondicherry French Quarter
notes: A neighbourhood of mustard-yellow colonial buildings, bougainvillea-covered walls and quiet, grid-like streets close to the sea. The mix of French and Tamil influences is visible in everything from the architecture to the street names.

name: Hussain Sagar Lake, Hyderabad
notes: A large artificial lake at the heart of Hyderabad, with a giant monolithic Buddha statue standing on an island in the middle. The promenade around it is a popular spot for evening walks and boat rides.

name: Charminar, Hyderabad
notes: A sixteenth-century monument with four grand arches and minarets, sitting at the centre of Hyderabad's old city. The surrounding lanes are packed with bangle markets, perfume shops and street food stalls.

name: Chowringhee Food Area, Kolkata
notes: A stretch of central Kolkata lined with old cafés, roadside stalls and classic Bengali sweet shops. It is easy to spend an entire afternoon moving between tea stalls and kathi roll vendors here.

name: Paranthe Wali Gali, Chandni Chowk, Delhi
notes: A narrow lane famous for generations-old shops serving stuffed parathas with a long list of fillings. The lane is barely wide enough for two people to pass, which only adds to its old-city charm.

name: Kulcha Land, Amritsar
notes: A cluster of small eateries known for stuffed kulchas served with spiced chickpeas and a generous dollop of butter. The simple tandoors and quick turnover of orders give the area a lively, no-frills energy.

name: Sarafa Bazaar, Indore
notes: A jewellery market by day that transforms into one of India's most famous night food streets after dark. Stalls selling garadu, bhutte ka kees and sweets stay busy well past midnight.

name: Aminabad Food Street, Lucknow
notes: An old market area known for kebabs, biryani and Awadhi sweets served from shops that have stayed in the same families for decades. The aroma from the tandoors tends to reach the street before the food itself does.

name: VV Puram Food Street, Bengaluru
notes: A compact lane in Basavanagudi lined with stalls serving South Indian snacks, chaats and sweets late into the night. It gets busy quickly after sunset, with most stalls specialising in just one or two dishes.

name: Pangong Tso Lake, Ladakh
notes: A high-altitude lake that changes colour through shades of blue and green depending on the time of day and angle of light. The stark, treeless mountains surrounding it make the water appear even more vivid.

name: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur
notes: A massive hilltop fort overlooking Jodhpur's blue-painted old city. The view from its ramparts at sunset, with the rooftops glowing below, is one of the more recognisable sights in Rajasthan.

name: Lotus Temple, Delhi
notes: A Bahá'í house of worship shaped like a blooming lotus flower, built from white marble petals arranged around a central hall. The structure looks different depending on whether it is seen against daylight or at dusk.

name: Munnar Tea Gardens, Kerala
notes: Rolling hills covered in neatly trimmed tea bushes, with mist often settling over the valleys in the early morning. The repeating green patterns make the landscape look almost sculpted from above.

name: Thiksey Monastery, Ladakh
notes: A multi-storeyed monastery built into a hillside, often compared to the Potala Palace for its tiered white-and-red structure. Morning prayers inside the main hall are accompanied by horns and chanting that carry out across the valley.

name: Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh
notes: A high-altitude cold desert valley with narrow mountain roads, ancient monasteries and some of the most dramatic landscapes in the Himalayas. The remoteness and unpredictable weather make every journey here feel like an expedition.

name: Auli, Uttarakhand
notes: A Himalayan hill station known for skiing in winter and wide meadow views in summer. A cable car ride up offers sweeping views of snow-capped peaks including Nanda Devi.

name: Coorg Trekking Trails, Karnataka
notes: A hilly coffee-growing region with trails that wind through plantations, forests and waterfalls. The cooler climate and varied terrain make it a popular base for both short hikes and multi-day treks.

name: Havelock Island, Andaman
notes: An island known for clear water, coral reefs and some of the best scuba diving sites in India. Radhanagar Beach here is often ranked among the finest beaches in Asia.

name: Khardung La Pass, Ladakh
notes: One of the highest motorable mountain passes in the world, connecting Leh to the Nubra and Shyok valleys. The thin air and sweeping views from the top make it a milestone for many road trips through Ladakh.

name: Alleppey Backwaters, Kerala
notes: A network of calm canals, lagoons and lakes lined with coconut palms, best explored slowly aboard a traditional houseboat. The quiet rhythm of life along the water makes it easy to understand why this place keeps drawing people back.

name: Baga Beach, Goa
notes: A lively stretch of coastline known for its beach shacks, water sports and relaxed evenings by the sea. It has a way of feeling familiar and new at the same time with every visit.

name: Shillong, Meghalaya
notes: A hill town often called the Scotland of the East, with rolling hills, waterfalls and a notably cool climate. The surrounding countryside, dotted with lakes and pine forests, makes it a place worth returning to in every season.

name: Leh, Ladakh
notes: A high-desert town surrounded by barren mountains and dotted with monasteries, palaces and market streets. The stark landscape and high altitude make it feel unlike anywhere else, and one visit rarely feels like enough.

name: Darjeeling, West Bengal
notes: A Himalayan hill town famous for its tea gardens, toy train and views of Kangchenjunga on clear mornings. The misty streets and colonial-era architecture give it a character worth experiencing across different seasons.

name: Mawlynnong Village, Meghalaya
notes: A small village known for its cleanliness, living root bridges and dense surrounding forest. The slow pace of life here stands in sharp contrast to most cities, making it a place that lingers in memory long after leaving.

name: Rajiv Chowk Metro Interchange, Delhi
notes: One of the busiest interchange stations on the Delhi Metro network, connecting two major lines beneath Connaught Place. The constant flow of commuters during peak hours offers a glimpse into the scale of the city's daily movement.

name: Howrah Bridge, Kolkata
notes: A cantilever bridge spanning the Hooghly River, carrying an enormous volume of pedestrian, vehicle and cycle traffic each day. Its structure, built without nuts or bolts, remains one of the busiest bridges in the world.

name: Statue of Unity Viewpoint, Gujarat
notes: The viewing gallery near the base of the world's tallest statue, offering wide views across the Narmada river valley. The scale of the surrounding infrastructure, including the dam and visitor facilities, makes it an interesting example of large public construction.

name: Dadar Suburban Rail Junction, Mumbai
notes: A major interchange on Mumbai's suburban rail network, where the Western and Central lines meet. The platforms see an extraordinary density of commuters during rush hour, reflecting the scale of the city's daily transit system.

name: Golden Quadrilateral Junction, Nagpur
notes: A key junction point along India's Golden Quadrilateral highway network, linking routes toward Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. The volume and variety of long-distance traffic passing through make it a notable point on the national road system.
